extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), installation commanders, CE contractors, and other personnel responsible for Army publications, broadcasting, and official web content
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for producing, approving, and distributing Army public affairs products (news releases, CE and AF publications, photography, broadcasting, and official web content), including notification procedures for NBC/NBC-type incidents. Covers editorial policy, advertising, contractor relationships, imagery rules, style, and required training/clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for NBC accidents/incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons making news releases on NBC accidents or incidents will notify, by the fastest means available, specified organizations depending on location (CONUS off-installation, on-installation, OCONUS) and include release content, circumstances, and actions taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific recipients: Commander, Movement Control Center (for CONUS off-installation), OASD (PA), OCPA (duty officer during off-hours via AOC), AMC PAO (and duty officer), FORSCOM PAO (via emergency operations center), PAO of nearest Army installation, PAO Surface Deployment and Distribution Command (for commercial carrier movements). If OCONUS, notify through chain of command to the NMCC. For biological/chemical accidents, notify OCPA by fastest means and include release content; OCPA will notify other organizations outside chain of command on a need-to-know basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas command release governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of information for NBC accidents/incidents on or off U.S. military installations overseas will be governed by applicable treaties, international agreements, host nation laws, Service-to-Service technical arrangements, and Army/UC plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army component may constitute a JIB coordinating through appropriate UC, Chief U.S. Mission, Department of State, and host nation authorities. Overseas commands will translate the announcements in appendix I into the host nation's language to ensure quick response and public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval for additional contingency releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Other releases or announcements (or modifications) may be included in nuclear accident/incident PA plans to suit local contingencies only if approval has been given in advance by the OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local modifications require prior OCPA approval to be added to preplanned announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct communications authorization in NBC incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: PA communications should parallel command channels but direct communication by the fastest means is authorized with the OCPA to expedite PA actions in NBC accidents/incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct comms are permitted to speed public affairs response, but coordination with OCPA is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary function of Army publications and electronic media
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary function is to support a commander's internal objectives by providing Armywide and local information, assisting commanders to identify/correct command problems, and acting as tools for two-way communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See appendix J for internal objectives; publications should be designed to support these functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free flow of news without censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a free flow of news and information to all DA personnel without censorship or news management; calculated withholding of unfavorable news is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/news policies must support the commander's responsibility to keep readership informed; withholding unfavorable news is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality, objectivity, and tasteful selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure news coverage is factual and objective; select news and headlines using good taste and avoid morbid, sensational, or alarming details unessential to factual reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and balance are paramount; avoid unnecessary sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish fact from opinion and identify opinion sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between fact and opinion, and when opinion is expressed, identify the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and balance in coverage are paramount; identification of opinions preserves credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear labeling of editorials vs commentaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctly identify editorials (command position) and commentaries (personal opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear to readers when content reflects official command stance versus an individual's viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of opinions and information sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute opinions and information sources; attribution is essential to credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit all material from nonlocal or external sources (Army News Service, AFIS, command news releases, other government agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source basis for news content
rubrics_metrics.description: Base news content on releases, reports, and materials provided by the DA, subordinate commands, newspaper staff members, and other Government agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit nonlocal/external sources appropriately; use reliable official inputs as foundation for news items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing published/broadcasted items to requestors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific published or broadcasted items to anyone who requests them after distribution; PAO may release specific items prior if determined to be in the best interests of the command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain access to distributed material; exercise discretion to release prior to distribution when justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic standards and contemporary design
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage Army publications and audiovisual material using the highest standards and principles of good journalism, conforming to local commander and higher HQ guidance, and employing contemporary design principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply professional journalism practices to enhance credibility and effectiveness of communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial policy objective to support mission performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Design editorial policies to improve Army personnel's ability to perform missions by keeping them informed of Army policies, programs, and the individual's role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should be practical and mission-supportive, focusing on helping readers perform their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance (libel, copyright, trademark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must conform to laws and regulations involving libel, copyright, and trademark use and follow AP Stylebook and media law guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also comply with U.S. Government printing and postal regulations; consult The Associated Press Stylebook and Briefing on Media Law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic readership surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct periodic readership surveys to assist commander's assessment of the value of internal information publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveys to inform editorial direction and measure effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial contributions from outside official channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial contributions may include articles/products produced outside official channels (e.g., stringers or local organizations) if legal permission is obtained and they do not violate the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure legal clearance and compliance with regulation before using outside contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylines and rank usage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may use bylines; using rank is optional but must be consistent in style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and maintain a consistent policy on bylines and rank display across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial sponsorship mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercially sponsored events may be mentioned with other pertinent facts in news stories if newsworthy and usage clearly meets Army needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to AR 215–1 chapter 7 for commercial sponsorship policy; include sponsor names only when appropriate to Army interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment reviews policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Book, radio, television, movie, restaurant, and other entertainment reviews may be included if there is no implication of DA selective benefit or endorsement; accepting gratuities in connection with reviews is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA staff may accept press credentials or passes, but not gratuities; avoid any appearance of endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preferential treatment for private organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: All private organizations approved to operate on the installation may have meetings announced and other material considered; no organization will receive preferential treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure equity in announcements, including veterans organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the editor editorial discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: CE and AF publication editors will edit letters to the editor at their discretion; commands are not obligated to respond to or return unsolicited editorial material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors have editorial control over letters and unsolicited submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on covering ongoing test/evaluation programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering ongoing test or evaluation programs is prohibited; exceptions require approval through channels to the OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow para 5–36 process for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising identification and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: All commercial advertising, including advertising supplements, must be clearly identified and labeled; paid advertorials must be labeled and distinguishable from editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure readers can readily distinguish advertising from editorial material; explicit labeling required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on endorsement and advertising practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications will not contain material implying Army endorsement of a commercial product/service; will not subscribe to commercial/feature wire services whose primary purpose is advertising; will not carry advertising that violates or rejects DA equal opportunity policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separation between Army and commercial promotion; enforce EO compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of color in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Color must be functional and add value; it will not be used just for color’s sake; PAOs should be sensitive to funding and degree to which color contributes to communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spot color or full-color processes per AR 25–30; CE publications limited by contract and contractor capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official imagery definition and quality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Official imagery includes all photographic/video images recorded or produced by persons acting for or on behalf of DOD activities; photographs in authorized publications must support PA goals and be of the highest photojournalistic quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographic reporting should visually communicate information with a journalistic view; historical/documentation photos are not a PA function; photos should show people performing their jobs and avoid 'grip and grin' clichés; comply with DA Pam 25–91 for disposition of visual info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on taking non-PA photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking photographs for promotion boards, ceremonies, changes of command, or social events, except for news publication, is not a PA function; non-PA photo requirements should be referred to Training/Visual Information Support Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish PA photography responsibilities from other documentation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration and postproduction rules for official imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: No one acting for the Department of the Army will alter official imagery except for specified permitted modifications; alterations that misrepresent the facts/circumstances are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: traditional darkroom/digital techniques (dodging, burning, color balancing, contrast adjustment), specialized techniques for authorized functions (cartography, intelligence, medical, RDT&E) if they do not misrepresent, masking for security/criminal investigation, cropping/editing/enlarging (unless misrepresenting), digital conversion/compression, and postproduction enhancements for dramatic/narrative effect if they do not misrepresent and it is clear from context that image is a representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CE publications: definition and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: CE publications (newspapers, magazines, guides, maps, Web sites) support internal communications; commander or PA office provides oversight and final approval authority for editorial content; CE contractors sell advertising to cover costs and secure earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriated or NAFs must not be used to pay CE contractor publishing costs; space allotment and oversight are defined in written contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial approval authority for CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Only material approved by the commander or PAO acting as the commander's representative may appear in the editorial portion of CE publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The printer may recommend material, but approval authority remains with command (may be delegated in writing but commander retains ultimate responsibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting and use of commercial news sources in CE/AF publications
rubrics_metrics.description: CE contracting guidelines are in DODI 5120.4; CE newspaper contracting is not subject to the FAR though commanders may opt to use FAR procedures. Using commercial news/opinion sources in DA publications is not normally authorized except under specified conditions and with OCPA authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army newspapers can use commercial news sources when other sources are not available and OCPA approves; waiver requests forwarded through channels to OCPA Newspaper Branch. Overseas UC newspapers have additional permissions and must ensure political campaign news is balanced and nonpartisan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor-military relationship boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Relationship between PA staff and CE contractor employees is government employees working with private contractor employees; supervising CE employees remains contractor responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military/DA civilian personnel will not be assigned duty on the CE contractor's premises or perform contractor business functions; PA staff may perform liaison functions to monitor layout/design per contract; PA staff will not supervise printer's employees; printer employees may seek technical guidance; terminals placed in PA office should be paid for by CE contractor who retains title and responsibility; conflicts of interest must be avoided and reported to servicing SJA.

rubrics_metrics.name: AF publications operational and distribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: AF newspapers and magazines support command communication requirements; normally printed by commercial printers under contract; editorial content and distribution by publishing command; distribution using appropriated funds and manpower may be authorized; expense charged to appropriated funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended minimum circulation ratio is one copy to three readers; AF and CE publications must comply with AR 340–21 and AR 25–51 distribution rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication name and trademarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication name may include command/installation name and emblem; use of Department of the Army emblem is prohibited except as authorized; commanders will trademark names of publications and ensure Army ownership of names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts should stipulate that the name is lent to the printer only for contract duration; contact Patents, Copyrights, and Trademarks Division for trademark info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masthead content and disclaimer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All publication mastheads will contain a disclaimer in no smaller than 6-point type and list names of commanding officer and PAO, editorial staff names/titles, a circulation figure, and office address/telephone of editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimer not required in CE guides and installation maps; names of publisher and publisher's employees may be listed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising review and commander authority over CE distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the CE contractor will use the agreed advertising space; PA staff reviews advertisements before printing to identify those contrary to law, posing danger, or interfering with missions. The CE contractor's ad acceptance decision is final, but commander may prohibit distribution of CE publications containing objectionable ads after legal coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAO may discuss publisher decisions but cannot substitute judgment; if objectionable ads printed, commander may prohibit on-post distribution; seek legal opinion and coordinate with legal staff before prohibiting distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on advertisements for games of chance
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements or editorial material about games of chance are prohibited except certain statutory exceptions (18 USC 1307, Indian Gaming Regulatory Act, nonprofit or government lotteries, occasional ancillary promotions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lottery defined by prize, chance, and consideration; exceptions do not apply to activities requiring no payment to play.

rubrics_metrics.name: News and editorial material approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Material to appear in editorial portion of CE publications will be provided to the printer and approved only by the commander or PA officer as commander's representative (authority may be delegated in writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper may publish civilian community news/announcements that benefit the readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: CE guide and map content and contracting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CE guidebooks intended primarily for newcomers; content should orient newcomers and families, include services/facilities info, pay/benefits, and quality-of-life photos/articles; CE maps intended for visitors and may be contracted as part of a package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include installation name and printer in disclaimer, phone numbers of service facilities allowed but not personal private info, biographies/photos of current military officials not included, coordinate with communications officer for format and security messages, table of contents must include printer info, editorial masthead required, printer solicitation materials must not include on-post address or military names, commander provides letter of authorization to printer specifying relationship, purpose, copy numbers, distribution, contact info, and contract expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm selection criteria for CE contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision to select a firm will be based on demonstrated potential to meet contract specifications; firms will not be selected based on inducements (audiovisual packages, stationery, VIP copies, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request or accept inducements; base selection on ability to meet regulation-written specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and usage conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: AF and CE publications should use a consistent style; AP Stylebook is preferred and Webster's New World Dictionary (or equivalent) preferred. Terms of reference include using last name only in subsequent references, referring to Soldiers by rank not pay grade, omitting rank in sports/competition stories, and capitalizing 'Soldier' and 'Families' when referring to U.S. Soldiers and Army Families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP Stylebook guidance for personal titles and subsequent reference; ensure consistent application across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcasting authorized materials and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: CONUS-based stations may use news, entertainment, and PA programs produced by Soldiers Radio and Television, commercial records/tapes with broadcast rights, commercial production/music packages procured properly, PA materials produced by ACOM HQ, promotional/no-cost programs, visual information produced/cleared per AR 25–1, and news services procured locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONUS stations are not authorized to use programming produced exclusively for AFRTS; acquisitions must follow DOD directives; authorization to use other DOD/Federal programming requested through channels to OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Web site publishing policies and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: All information on a publicly accessible Web site is public information and subject to this regulation's policies and clearance procedures and must comply with AR 25–1, AR 25–2, AR 340–21, AR 380–5, AR 530–1, DODD 5230.09, DODI 5230.29, and JP 3–13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official Web sites must have a clearly defined purpose and Web site plan approved by the commander/director; post only information of value to visitors; include social media in PA planning; official Web sites must not contain nonreleasable information (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonreleasable web content (prohibited on official sites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Web sites or blogs must not have information considered nonreleasable under FOIA: classified information; casualty info before NOK notified; Privacy Act-protected info; info regarding ongoing investigations; imagery of U.S. Coalition Forces without release or enemy personnel casualties; information that misrepresents the Army or conflicts with good order/morale/discipline; sensitive photographs (IED results, battle scenes, casualties, destroyed equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully screen web content for these categories; err on side of withholding until clearance/verification obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web site posting training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PA officials responsible for posting unclassified information to official Web sites must complete the Web site training course offered through https://iatraining.us.army.mil; this also applies to Soldiers, DA civilians, and supporting contractors who review, post, and maintain Army content on non-Army.mil Web sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required personnel complete the mandated training before posting public web content.
